A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CoMeT study and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices. Existing material can be matched across relocation and renumbering, including the retained appendix analyses and gating visualizations.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, passkey retrieval experiments, memory ablations, and inference-efficiency measurements in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those results and adds original evaluations across model backbones, long-document extrapolation tests, hyperparameter ablations, an efficiency comparison, and failure cases.

M1.justification: The chunk-processing procedure, residual low-rank adapters, gated global memory, FIFO temporary memory, and layer-level pipeline parallelism remain unchanged. The added scheduling illustration and hyperparameter experiments document and evaluate the existing method.

E1.justification: v2 extends length-extrapolation evaluation from synthetic passkey retrieval to realistic GovReport and NarrativeQA inputs exceeding the 32k training length, reaching 484k tokens (Appendix D). Table 9 also adds NQ and NarrativeQA evaluations explicitly distinguished from SCROLLS. Original task coverage is retained.

E2.justification: Appendix G adds RWKV-7-Goose-World-2.9B-HF as an efficiency comparator; v1's efficiency comparisons used Full Attention. Comparator membership in the original Tables 2–4 is unchanged.

E3.justification: New evaluation configurations include Qwen3-14B and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, a 4,854-example SCROLLS subset above 32k tokens, and sweeps over adapter rank, chunk size, compression interval, and temporary-memory budget. The existing training settings remain unchanged; the agent experiment already used Qwen3-8B in v1.

E4.justification: v2 adds substantial analyses of backbone generalization, realistic length extrapolation, adapter-rank sensitivity, and chunk/compression/memory choices (Tables 5–7 and 9). Appendix J adds four Qasper failure cases examining detail loss, causal reasoning, and information aggregation. Existing memory ablations and gating analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable uncertainty estimates. The added tables continue reporting point estimates.

E6.justification: Original Tables 2–4 retain their numerical results. Substantial new results include CoMeT SCROLLS averages of 43.14 on Qwen3-14B and 40.55 on Llama-3.1-8B, and long-subset NarrativeQA F1 of 13.2 versus SWA's 5.8. Tables 6 and 8–10 add sensitivity scores, runtime measurements, and qualitative failure outcomes under additional settings.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, RLA and gated-update equations, and complexity reasoning remain unchanged. The new pipeline diagram and empirical analyses introduce no new formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The introduction narrows the claim that overall performance surpasses existing efficient methods to achieving the highest average score among the methods evaluated. The abstract and conclusion retain the same principal architecture, complexity, extrapolation, and application claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations of model-dependent performance, the remaining Full Attention advantage on long documents, and RWKV7's prefill/memory tradeoff. Appendix J offers compression-related explanations for Qasper failures and qualifies their uniqueness. A new societal-impact section discusses privacy risks tied to processing user histories; the original limitations paragraph remains.

D1.justification: v2 changes the advertised code location from an anonymous host to a named GitHub repository. It additionally documents the 3.95M-parameter overhead, xRAG's vector encoding, 5–7-digit passkeys, and RWKV implementation details and kernel limitations. These disclosures do not establish changes to the retained experiments.

R1.justification: The bibliography and Related Work section are unchanged. The introduction qualifies its previously categorical criticism of context compression to typical settings, while Appendix G adds direct positioning against RWKV7's efficiency tradeoffs.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main narrative structure are retained. Changes include localized wording clarifications, expanded abbreviations and affiliation information, additional analysis subsections, ethics and acknowledgments sections, and reorganized appendix labels.

P2.justification: v2 adds six tables covering generalization, extrapolation, sensitivity, efficiency, and failure cases, plus a pipeline execution diagram. Existing illustrations and tables are repositioned, and captions gain clarification. The original graphics are retained, including the all-layer gating visualization renumbered from Figure 11 to Figure 12.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation of the existing method: additional backbones and realistic extrapolation tests address important gaps left by v1's predominantly single-backbone academic evaluation and synthetic extrapolation evidence. The new ablations and failure analyses make design choices and limitations more assessable, including the remaining Full Attention gap and RWKV7 prefill advantage. Although statistical uncertainty remains unreported, the broader evidence provides a substantial overall quality gain.
